Descriptive means/SDs and regression coefficients/SEs are present in this PDF, Appendix A (pp. 34-36) and Appendix B (pp. 37-53). Additional statistics in the external supplement are unverified: Python urllib requests to the named OSF supplement and preregistration were blocked by socket access restrictions (WinError 10013).

paper_design_summary: Experiment I randomly allocated 435 professionals and college students to 122 teams, then randomized teams to no AI, one ChatGPT4.0 touchpoint per team, or one per member (pp. 8-9). Teams completed article-writing and retail-strategy tasks, and six blind online judges rated each output on overall quality, novelty and usefulness (p. 10). Experiment II analyzed 139 individuals doing the same tasks with ChatGPT4.0 and compared their outputs with the Experiment I teams without random assignment between individuals and teams; whether any individuals had participated in Experiment I is not stated (p. 11).

task.description: Two professional tasks per team: (1) a content-generation task writing a series of in-depth articles on college students' job hunting and career development; (2) a strategy-development task designing a digital transformation strategy for a traditional retail chain (p. 9). sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: No other paper is identified as sharing participants. Within this paper, Experiment II reuses the 122 Experiment I teams as comparators and analyzes 139 individuals in its individual-AI arm. Whether any of those individuals had participated in Experiment I is not stated; the number of additional unique people across the two experiments is unconfirmed (p. 11, Section 2.2; p. 36, Appendix A Table 3).

eligibility.reason: Experiment I independently meets all three criteria. Teams were randomly assigned to generative-AI access or no AI (p. 9, Section 2.1; p. 26, Figure 1). The 435 participants were allocated to 122 distinct teams of three to five members (pp. 8-9), and all 122 teams are represented in the analyzed 244-output dataset (pp. 10-11; p. 34, Appendix A Table 1). These distinct human teams establish that more than 50 people contributed to the analyzed outputs; an exact analyzed headcount is not separately printed and remains null. Blind judges rated the produced articles and strategies on novelty, overall quality and usefulness, with AI available during production in the AI arms (pp. 9-10). Reported robust output-level SEs do not establish adjustment for repeated outputs within teams, so precision suitable for pooling remains unverified. Experiment II is a nonrandomized individual-versus-team comparison using the Experiment I teams as comparators (p. 11; p. 21) and is context only (quasi_people/observational). Its 139 analyzed individuals are not added to the randomized sample; their possible overlap with Experiment I is unreported and does not affect eligibility.

one_line_finding: AI-assisted teams scored higher on quality (0.417, SE 0.148) and novelty (0.344, SE 0.150), with a weaker usefulness gain (0.250, SE 0.150; p < .10) and no clear advantage from multiple AI touchpoints (pp. 37-39, Appendix B Tables 1-3).
open_questions: Exact analyzed headcounts for Experiment I and its reused team comparators are not separately printed; assignment counts are not relabeled analyzed counts (pp. 8-11, 34).
Experiment II occupation/student composition is not stated; population is null (p. 11; pp. 35-36).
Both named OSF sources failed with WinError 10013. External supplement statistics and preregistered outcome priority remain unverified.

Bayesian multiple-versus-single-AI estimates conflict between p. 13 and Appendix B Table 4 (p. 40): overall quality text -0.072 [-0.303, 0.169], table -0.024 [-0.273, 0.200]; novelty text 0.025 [-0.220, 0.262], table 0.094 [-0.170, 0.367]; usefulness text 0.076 [-0.184, 0.323], table 0.065 [-0.154, 0.296]. Both versions are preserved; the PDF cannot establish a corrected estimate.
The time-controlled AI-team novelty result has p > .05 in the text (p. 18), but Appendix B Table 9 (p. 45) prints 0.372** (0.147), with ** defined as p < 0.05. The source contradiction is preserved.
The units/transformation of completion time and a task time limit are not stated (pp. 17-19; p. 43).
The PDF reports robust output-level SEs without stating team/participant clustering (pp. 37-39, 42, 45, 47-48); independent-unit precision for pooling is unverified.
No arXiv version or document date is printed; PDF creation metadata does not verify that the saved version is latest.

Whether any of the 139 analyzed Experiment II individuals previously participated in Experiment I is not stated; no additional unique-person count across experiments is established (p. 11, Section 2.2; p. 36, Appendix A Table 3).
notes: Read the complete markdown conversion, including references and Appendices A-B; retained numbers were checked against PDF text. Both forms list the same three output dimensions per study. Quality is usefulness under the codebook. Mixed article-writing/strategy tasks are coded other and qualify because novelty is judged on output. All retained outcomes answer with_ai; relative distributions of rating scores are not semantic diversity across people. No after_ai outcome is reported. Human-only teams received AI after submitting the analyzed outputs; refinement was excluded (p. 9, footnote 4). Completion time (pp. 17-19; Tables 7-8), team-process self-reports (p. 10; Tables 16-17), and interaction measures (pp. 19-20; Tables 13-15) are not additional eligible output outcomes. The self-reported potency and satisfaction coefficients noted only by B are 0.313** (0.149) and 0.266* (0.149) (p. 52, Table 16), but are excluded. Heterogeneity and relative-distribution analyses concern the same ratings. SDs and regression Ns are output-level, not person-level. Pooled AI combines the two randomized AI arms; it is not another randomized arm. No effect sizes, headcounts, pooled means/SDs, or direct contrasts were calculated. Reconciliation counts cover substantive cross-form differences; shared source discrepancies and further gaps are in open_questions. Locators use one-based PDF pages. Finalization re-read the complete markdown, including Appendices A-B, and verified the retained numbers against PDF text. The people challenge was corrected by removing unsupported claims that the Experiment II individuals were additional unique participants. The reconciliation object is preserved as the historical record; its earlier new-participant wording is superseded by final.challenge_resolution. Python urllib requests with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 to both named OSF sources again failed with WinError 10013; no external supplement or preregistration contents were verified.

challenge_resolution.what_changed: Reworded sample_overlap, the S2 participant and individual-arm descriptions, paper_design_summary, S2 assignment and eligibility.reason to report 139 analyzed individuals with unknown overlap with Experiment I. Retained the supported counts of 139 individuals and 278 outputs. Added the overlap question to open_questions and final.open_items; no cross-experiment unique-person total is asserted. open_items.item: Exact analyzed headcounts for Experiment I overall and by arm, including its human-only and pooled-AI teams reused in Experiment II, are unreported (pp. 8-11, 34). An explicit participant-flow statement from the authors would settle the three unresolved reconciliation entries on these counts. Criterion 2 is already met by the analyzed outputs from 122 distinct human teams.

Experiment II occupation/student composition remains unstated (p. 11; pp. 35-36), as recorded in open_questions and the unresolved population reconciliation entry. An author description of the recruitment population would settle the category; population category is not an eligibility criterion.

Additional external supplement statistics remain unverified (source.supplement.holds and its unresolved reconciliation entry). Access to the OSF supplement linked on p. 8 would settle its contents; the saved PDF already documents the design and output ratings and includes the main descriptive and regression tables. Both named OSF requests failed with WinError 10013.

Preregistered outcome priority is unverified because the OSF registration linked on p. 4 was inaccessible. Access to that supplementary protocol would settle priority; preregistered primary status is not one of the three eligibility criteria.

The multiple-versus-single-AI Bayesian means and credible intervals differ between p. 13 and Appendix B Table 4 (p. 40). Both printed versions are preserved. Author confirmation of the intended estimates would settle the conflict; it concerns results rather than any eligibility criterion.

The time-controlled AI-team novelty p-value contradicts its significance marker between p. 18 and Appendix B Table 9 (p. 45). Author confirmation of the intended p-value would settle the conflict; significance does not determine eligibility.

The task time limit and completion-time units/transformation remain unstated (pp. 17-19; p. 43), including the unresolved task.duration reconciliation entry. The authors could supply the task instructions and time-variable definition. These details affect interpretation of time-adjusted analyses, not the three eligibility criteria.

Team/participant clustering is not stated for the robust output-level SEs (pp. 37-39, 42, 45, 47-48). Analysis code or output data with team/participant identifiers would permit checking the SE basis or obtaining independent-unit precision. This affects pooling, not core screening eligibility.

The saved PDF prints no version number or document date; creation metadata does not establish that it is latest. An identified journal version or dated latest document would settle version provenance and permit comparison. No version-dependent uncertainty about the three criteria is identified in the saved PDF.

Whether Experiment II individuals had previously participated in Experiment I is unknown (p. 11; p. 36). An explicit author statement about cross-experiment participation would settle overlap. Experiment I independently meets all criteria, and the individual count is not added to its randomized sample.
